intro: In a dissertation, an article or a research report, it is word partnerships (“conduct research”, “draw a conclusion”, “a significant difference”) that make a text sound right. Perfect grammar is not enough if the collocations are translated from another language.
objectifs: Use the main verb + noun collocations of research (conduct a study, collect data, draw a conclusion, address an issue).
Choose the expected adjective and adverb (a significant difference, closely related, widely accepted).
Use the right preposition after key nouns (an increase in, an impact on, research into).
Avoid typical learner mistakes (make a research, an important number of, realise a study).

texte: A collocation is a combination of words that native speakers use habitually. Logically nothing stops you saying “make a conclusion”, but English says “draw / reach a conclusion”. Readers notice the difference at once, and the text loses credibility.

In academic English, four types dominate: verb + noun (conduct research), adjective + noun (compelling evidence), adverb + adjective or verb (closely linked, clearly demonstrate) and noun + preposition (an increase in). Learn them as chunks, with an example.
exemples: We conducted a survey of 500 households.
“Conduct”: the neutral, formal verb for a survey or study.
The study draws three main conclusions.

sections.titre: Verb + noun: doing research and arguing
texte: These collocations describe the stages of research: designing, collecting, analysing, concluding and discussing. “Do research” is possible in speech, but “conduct” or “carry out” is preferred in writing.

lignes: conduct / carry out research, a study, an experiment, a survey
The team carried out a series of experiments.
Data were collected over six months.
put forward / test / support / reject a hypothesis
The results support our initial hypothesis.
The study provides strong evidence of a link.
raise / address / tackle an issue; pose a problem / a threat
This chapter addresses the issue of access.
Education plays a crucial role in mobility.
draw / reach / come to a conclusion
It is too early to draw firm conclusions.
shed / throw light on; fill / bridge a gap (in the literature)
This paper fills a gap in the literature.

exemples: Several questions are raised by these findings.
The report fails to address the issue of cost.
“Address an issue” = deal with it (academic meaning of address).

texte: An academic adjective is chosen for precision, not intensity. “A big difference” is informal; “a significant difference” is expected (and in statistics means the difference is not due to chance).
The words “evidence”, “research” and “data” have their usual adjectives: compelling / conclusive / limited evidence, extensive / recent research, reliable / limited data.

lignes: There is conflicting evidence on this point.
We found a marked difference between groups.
There was a sharp decline in enrolment.
Price is a key factor in consumer choice.
There is a broad consensus among economists.
a growing / large body of research / evidence
A growing body of research links sleep and memory.

exemples: A growing body of evidence suggests that the policy is effective.

texte: Adverbs “stick” to certain adjectives and verbs. We say “closely related”, “widely used” and “highly significant”, but not “highly used”.

lignes: Income is closely linked to education.
This model is widely used in finance.
not likely to be due to chance
The difference is not statistically significant.
The rise is largely due to inflation.
The region is heavily dependent on tourism.
clearly demonstrate / critically examine / briefly outline
show clearly / examine carefully and critically / describe in a few words
This section briefly outlines the method.

exemples: Unemployment is closely linked to the level of qualification.

texte: The preposition after an academic noun must be learnt. “An increase of 5 %” gives the amount; “an increase in prices” gives what changes. Also: the impact on, research into / on.

lignes: the effect of stress on memory
evidence of fraud / evidence for a theory
We examine the extent to which age matters.
in terms of, with respect to, on the basis of, in contrast to
On the basis of these results, we recommend…

exemples: The report measures the impact of the reform on small businesses.
impact OF the reform ON small businesses.

texte: “Research”, “evidence”, “information” and “advice” are uncountable: no “researches”, “evidences” or “informations”. To count, say “a study”, “studies”, “a piece of evidence”.
“Data” is a Latin plural: “the data show” is standard in many scientific journals, but “the data shows” (uncountable) is now very common and accepted. Be consistent throughout your text.

False friends: “realise” = become aware (to carry out a study: conduct); “an experience” = something you live through (a scientific test = an experiment); “important” does not describe a quantity (an important number → a large number).
exemples: Two recent studies confirm this result.
To count pieces of research, use “studies”, not “researches”.
The data show / The data shows a clear trend.
Both are used; choose one and keep it throughout the text.

formule: Verb + noun (conduct a study, draw a conclusion) · adjective + noun (a significant difference) · adverb + adjective (closely linked) · noun + preposition (an increase in, an impact on)
prononciation: “conduct” changes stress: the verb is /kənˈdʌkt/ (second syllable), the noun /ˈkɒndʌkt/ (first syllable).
“research” is /rɪˈsɜːtʃ/ (BrE, stressed on the second syllable); in American English the noun is also often /ˈriːsɜːrtʃ/.
“analyse” (BrE) / “analyze” (AmE) is /ˈænəlaɪz/; the noun “analysis” /əˈnæləsɪs/ moves the stress.
erreurs: We made a research on migration.
We conducted research into / on migration.
“Research” is uncountable and goes with conduct / carry out.
An important number of students failed.
A large / significant number of students failed.
“Important” does not measure quantity in English.
We realised a study in 2024.
We conducted / carried out a study in 2024.
“Realise” = become aware.
They did an experience in the lab.
They carried out an experiment in the lab.
A scientific test is an experiment.
We can make the conclusion that…
We can draw the conclusion that… / We can conclude that…
You “draw” a conclusion.
There are many evidences of a link.
There is a great deal of evidence of a link.
“Evidence” is uncountable.
The increase of prices was sharp.
The increase in prices was sharp.
“Increase in” + what rises; “of” + the amount.
This rises an important question.
This raises an important question.
“Raise” (transitive) ≠ “rise” (intransitive).

dialogue.contexte: At the University of Buea, a PhD student goes through the introduction of her article with her supervisor.
lignes: Your first sentence says “We made a research on mobile banking.” Let's fix that.
Correct verb, uncountable noun, right preposition.
Perfect. And “an important number of users”?
“A significant number of users”… or “a large number”, since it's not a statistical test.
She thinks about the statistical meaning of “significant”.
Good thinking. Then you write that mobile money “has a big role”.
It “plays a crucial role in financial inclusion”.
Exactly. And how would you describe your contribution?
“This paper fills a gap in the literature and sheds light on rural users.”
Excellent. Now it sounds like a real journal article.

mots: facts that show something is true (uncountable)
large or important enough to notice; (statistics) not due to chance
There is no consensus on this issue.
We found a strong correlation between the variables.
a connection between two things that change together
We measure the extent to which prices changed.
The study is based on empirical data.

exercices.consigne: Choose the verb that forms the correct collocation.
items: to ___ light on a problem (throw / give)

exercices.titre: 2. Complete with the adjective or adverb
exercices.consigne: Complete with: growing, closely, widely, sharp, conflicting, significant.
items: There was a ___ decline in sales in March.
This method is ___ used in medicine.
A ___ body of research supports this view.
Studies have produced ___ evidence on this point.
The difference between the two groups was not statistically ___.
the impact of social media ___ teenagers
We made a research on rural schools.
We conducted research into / on rural schools.
An important number of patients improved.
A large / significant number of patients improved.
The researchers did an experience on mice.
The researchers carried out an experiment on mice.

exercices.consigne: Rewrite each sentence with an academic collocation.
items: It's too early to say anything for sure.
It is too early to draw firm conclusions.
This rise is mainly because of inflation.
This increase is largely due to inflation.

exercices.consigne: Write a short paragraph (4 sentences) presenting a real or imaginary study. Use at least five collocations from the lesson.
items: We conducted a survey of 800 small farmers in the West Region in order to examine the impact of mobile money on savings. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews and analysed using regression models. The findings show a significant increase in savings among users, which is largely due to lower transaction costs. These results shed light on an area that has received little attention, although further research is needed.

a_retenir: Learn collocations as chunks: conduct a study, collect data, draw a conclusion, address an issue, play a role.
Precise rather than intense adjectives: a significant difference, a sharp decline, compelling evidence, a growing body of research.
Prepositions: an increase in, an impact on, research into, an approach to, the extent to which.
Uncountable: research, evidence, information; false friends: realise, experience, important (for a quantity).
